meta.method: Asset figures are copied from myneta.info (ADR) candidate pages, which summarise the self-sworn election affidavit. Totals are myneta's 'Total Assets' and 'Liabilities' lines (myneta sums self, spouse, HUF and dependants, movable plus immovable). Events come only from the news and legal reports opened during this research, each linked. 'Rs crore' is rounded to 2 decimals.
meta.caveat: Declared assets are self-reported at market or book value chosen by the candidate. Increases include revaluation of land and business holdings and of the spouse's and family's holdings. They are not proof of wrongdoing. No court has convicted D.K. Shivakumar or D.K. Suresh in any case listed here.

assets.note: Not found on myneta; see gaps.

assets.election: Lok Sabha by-election 2013 (Bangalore Rural, polled 21-08-2013; myneta site 'lsbye2012')

growth.note: Computed only from the declared totals above. Declared wealth includes revaluation of land and business holdings and family holdings; growth in declared assets is not proof of wrongdoing.

events.event: The Income Tax Department searched about 39 properties linked to then Energy Minister D.K. Shivakumar and his brother D.K. Suresh, including his room at Eagleton resort, where Gujarat Congress MLAs were staying before the 8 Aug Rajya Sabha poll.
events.established: Searches took place on 2 Aug 2017 at premises linked to both brothers and the resort, per contemporaneous reports.
events.not_established: Cash figures were reported unofficially (an unnamed investigator cited about Rs 5 crore in Delhi); later reports vary (Rs 7 crore to Rs 8.59 crore). Congress called the searches a political witch-hunt; that motive is an allegation, not a finding.
events.quote: It is now becoming a trend to blatantly misuse the powers of the state. (Congress MP Anand Sharma)

events.event: A special court discharged Shivakumar in three Income Tax prosecutions arising from the 2017 searches; the Karnataka High Court dismissed the department's challenge in April 2021.
events.established: The High Court (Justice John Michael Cunha) held the prosecution was invalid under the CrPC and Income Tax Act; Shivakumar stands discharged in those three cases.
events.not_established: The discharge was on procedural/jurisdictional grounds, not a finding on whether tax was evaded. The special court date (28 Feb 2019) and the reserved liberty to refile come from search-result summaries of other reports, not the article opened. Whether a fresh prosecution was filed was not found.
events.quote: prosecution initiated against Shivakumar was bad in law

events.event: The Enforcement Directorate arrested D.K. Shivakumar under the money-laundering law (PMLA) in a case that grew out of the 2017 Income Tax searches.
events.established: Arrest by ED on 3 Sep 2019 is on record.
events.not_established: The ED's allegations of hawala transactions were never tested at trial; the case was later quashed (see 2024-03-05).
events.quote: transactions involving huge amounts of unaccounted money on a regular basis through 'hawala' channels (ED's allegation, as reported)

events.event: The Delhi High Court (Justice Suresh Kait) granted Shivakumar bail in the ED case, and he was released from Tihar Jail that evening.
events.established: Bail granted 23 Oct 2019 by the Delhi High Court. Search-result summaries (not opened) also report the Supreme Court dismissed ED's challenge to the bail on 15 Nov 2019.
events.not_established: Bail is not a ruling on guilt or innocence.

events.event: The CBI registered a disproportionate-assets FIR alleging Shivakumar and family held about Rs 74.93 crore beyond known income for 1 Apr 2013 to 30 Apr 2018, and searched 14 locations on 5 Oct 2020.
events.established: The FIR was registered and searches were held, on consent given by the then BJP state government in Sept 2019.
events.not_established: The Rs 74.93 crore figure is the CBI's allegation. No chargesheet outcome or court finding on it was found. Shivakumar denies the allegations; his family's counsel called the action politically motivated.
events.quote: disproportionate assets amounting to Rs 74,93, 40, 069 (CBI's allegation, as reported)

events.event: The Congress state cabinet withdrew the previous government's consent for the CBI probe, and a state order of 26 Dec 2023 referred the DA case to the Karnataka Lokayukta.
events.established: Consent withdrawal and the Lokayukta referral are state decisions on record.
events.not_established: Whether the withdrawal is legally valid is still before the Supreme Court. Some reports date the decision 28 Nov 2023; Outlook gives 23 Nov.

events.event: The Supreme Court (Justices Surya Kant and K.V. Viswanathan) quashed the 2018 ED money-laundering proceedings against Shivakumar and an aide.
events.established: PMLA proceedings quashed because the only predicate offence cited (IPC 120B conspiracy) was not itself a scheduled offence, following the Pavana Dibbur ruling.
events.not_established: This was a legal ruling on the basis for the case, not a finding on the facts. LiveLaw noted ED had sought review of Pavana Dibbur, which could reopen the question; no such reopening was found.
events.quote: In view of the Pavana Dibbur decision, the reasons assigned by high court in impugned judgment cannot sustain.

events.event: D.K. Suresh lost the Bangalore Rural Lok Sabha seat to BJP's Dr C.N. Manjunath by 2,69,647 votes.
events.quote: Eminent cardiologist and former Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda's son-in-law Dr C N Manjunath of BJP won the seat.

events.event: The Supreme Court dismissed Shivakumar's plea to quash the CBI's DA FIR, declining to interfere with the High Court's 19 Oct 2023 order.
events.established: The FIR was not quashed by the courts.
events.not_established: Refusing to quash an FIR is not a finding of guilt.

events.event: The Karnataka High Court held the CBI's challenge to the state's withdrawal of consent non-maintainable, said the Supreme Court should decide it, and dismissed the plea against the Lokayukta referral.
events.established: The CBI challenge was dismissed on maintainability; the Lokayukta referral stands.
events.not_established: The court did not rule on the merits of the DA allegation.
events.quote: the issues raised in the petition should be addressed by the Supreme Court.

events.event: Hearing appeals by the CBI and BJP MLA Basangouda Patil Yatnal, the Supreme Court declined interim orders on the Lokayukta probe and sought the state's reply.
events.established: The appeals are pending; no interim stay of the Lokayukta investigation.
events.not_established: Yatnal's counsel claimed a Lokayukta closure report was likely; that is a litigant's claim, not a finding.
events.quote: Are we so powerless that we can't declare one proceeding annulled and allow the other to continue? (Justice Surya Kant)

events.event: The Supreme Court adjourned the consent-withdrawal appeals, questioning Yatnal's motives, pending the state's counter-affidavit.
events.established: Matter pending; next date listed as 26 March (2025).
events.not_established: No final ruling found in any source opened up to 13 Nov 2026.
events.quote: Why you are, for political mileage, before the Supreme Court?

events.event: Former MP D.K. Suresh appeared before the ED after a summons in its money-laundering probe of Aishwarya Gowda, accused of cheating a jeweller of gold worth Rs 9.82 crore.
events.established: Suresh was summoned for questioning and appeared.
events.not_established: The report does not say he is an accused. He denied any financial dealings with her. No outcome found.
events.quote: The ED has summoned me for questioning. I will fully cooperate and seek clarity on the grounds for the summons.

events.event: A Bengaluru court let Shivakumar travel abroad for two years under a bail condition in an Income Tax Department tax-evasion case that remains before the trial court.
events.established: An I-T case (Income Tax Department vs D K Shivakumar & others) was still pending as of May 2026, with Shivakumar on bail.
events.not_established: Charges and sections were not in the article opened; no verdict. This appears separate from the three prosecutions discharged in 2019/2021.
events.quote: allowed Karnataka Minister DK Shivakumar to travel abroad over a two-year period

events.event: D.K. Shivakumar was sworn in as Chief Minister of Karnataka, succeeding Siddaramaiah.
events.established: Oath administered by Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot at Lok Bhavan, Bengaluru, on 3 June 2026.
events.quote: Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot administered the oath of office and secrecy to Shivakumar at Lok Bhavan in Bengaluru.

gaps: 2004 (Sathanur) declared assets: myneta's Karnataka 2004 site could not be found (karnataka2004 is empty; kar2004 is a 404). Check the ECI affidavit archive or the ADR 2004-2008 comparison PDF before using any 2004 figure.

CBI's FIR puts Shivakumar's assets at Rs 33.9 crore on 1 Apr 2013, while the 2013 myneta total (self+spouse+dependants+HUF) is Rs 251.5 crore. The two use different scopes and valuations; do not put them side by side without explaining that.

Current status of the DA case: no Supreme Court ruling on the consent-withdrawal appeals, and no Lokayukta closure or chargesheet, was found in any source opened after Jan 2025. Treat it as pending; confirm on the Supreme Court case-status page before publishing.
The 2026 pending I-T tax-evasion case: exact charges and how it relates to the three discharged 2019 cases are unconfirmed.
Cash seized in the 2017 searches: reported figures range from Rs 5 crore to Rs 8.59 crore; only the unofficial Rs 5 crore figure is in the article opened.
Supreme Court dismissal of ED's bail challenge (15 Nov 2019) and the special court discharge date (28 Feb 2019) come from search summaries, not opened articles.
D.K. Suresh: no court case against him personally with an outcome was found; his own statement that 'ED cases against us' were closed (Hans India) was not opened or verified.
Nov 2023 consent withdrawal date: 23 Nov (Outlook, cabinet decision) vs 28 Nov (other reports, possibly the order date).
Deccan Herald pages returned HTTP 403 and were not used.
